name: aeval_sub_mem_of_gaussFiltration
summary: Induction on f: constants, adding a monomial, and multiplying by a variable; the filtration is multiplicative.

steps.claim: Induction on f (constants; adding a monomial not in the support; multiplying by a variable x_i), for all levels t.
steps.lean:
induction' f using induction_on'' with _ α x f e _ _ _ p i I generalizing t
  simpa using y (h 0)
  simp_all [add_sub_add_comm, add_mem_cancel_left,
    monomial_mem_gaussFiltration (by simpa [f.notMem_support_iff.1 e] using h α)]
  have ⟨a, b⟩ := @I (t - c i) (by grind [weight_single, coeff_mul_X, h <| · + single i 1])
  grind [mul_mem_graded a (add_mem (u i) (antitone (by simp) (v i))),
    add_mem (mul_mem_graded b (u i)) (antitone (by grind) (mul_mem_graded a (v i)))]

steps.claim: f = C(a): ψ(f) = χ(f) = image of a, which lies in G_t by y since a = f_0 ∈ F_{t − 0} (h at 0); the difference is 0.

f = monomial α x + f' with α not in the support of f': the coefficient x = f_α lies in F_{t − c·α} (h at α), so the monomial is in the filtration; with the induction hypotheses for the monomial and for f', both claims follow by additivity.
steps.lean:
simp_all [add_sub_add_comm, add_mem_cancel_left,
    monomial_mem_gaussFiltration (by simpa [f.notMem_support_iff.1 e] using h α)]

steps.claim: f = p·x_i: p lies in the Gauss filtration at level t − c(i) (its coefficients shift by c(i)), so by the induction hypothesis I at t − c(i): ψ(p) ∈ G_{t−c(i)} (a) and ψ(p) − χ(p) ∈ G_{t−c(i)+1/20} (b). Then ψ(p x_i) = ψ(p)·(χ(x_i) + (ψ − χ)(x_i)) ∈ G_t and ψ(p)ψ(x_i) − χ(p)χ(x_i) = ψ(p)(ψ − χ)(x_i) + (ψ − χ)(p)χ(x_i) ∈ G_{t+1/20}, by multiplicativity and antitonicity of G.
steps.lean:
have ⟨a, b⟩ := @I (t - c i) (by grind [weight_single, coeff_mul_X, h <| · + single i 1])
  grind [mul_mem_graded a (add_mem (u i) (antitone (by simp) (v i))),
    add_mem (mul_mem_graded b (u i)) (antitone (by grind) (mul_mem_graded a (v i)))]
